title.value: Early Transcriptional Changes in Rabies Virus-Infected Neurons and Their Impact on Neuronal Functions
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning and throughout the paper, accurately representing the focus of the study.
title.quote: Early Transcriptional Changes in Rabies Virus-Infected Neurons and Their Impact on Neuronal Functions

analysis.description: This paper investigates the early transcriptional changes in neurons infected with the rabies virus and examines how these changes impact neuronal functions. The study focuses on the role of the rabies virus matrix protein in modulating host gene expression and its implications on neuronal dysfunction.

type.justification: The research involves experimental procedures on human differentiated neurons infected with rabies virus, followed by RNA sequencing and data analysis to understand transcriptional changes.
type.quote: In this study, we used differentiated neurons to characterize the RABV-induced transcriptomic changes at the early time-points of infection.

name.justification: The paper deals extensively with rabies virus, focusing on virological aspects of how the virus impacts neuronal functions.
name.quote: This article was submitted to Virology, a section of the journal Frontiers in Microbiology.

name.justification: The study's focus is on neuronal functions and how the rabies virus affects these through transcriptional changes.
name.quote: Rabies virus-infected post-mortem brains do not show significant signs of inflammation nor the structural damages on neurons... the observed neurological symptoms possibly originate from dysfunctions of neurons.

name.justification: The paper examines transcriptional changes induced by rabies virus infection in neurons.
name.quote: We used differentiated neurons to characterize the RABV-induced transcriptomic changes at the early time-points of infection.
